name: Yara Solune
title: Sister
role: A missionary of the Quiet at Haven Station
note: Her skin holds a steady glow of perfect peace, and it frightens people more than anger would.
appearance: A slim Ilari in plain grey, whose skin holds one slow, even glow of pure white that never changes, not in a firefight, and not when someone spits at her. Other Ilari cross the dock to avoid her.
personality: Serene, patient and attentive to frightened people, in a way that looks like compassion. She's never angry and never in a hurry. She is not at peace. She has lost the part of her that could be anything else, and she stays close to frightened people the way you'd hold your hands out to a fire.
voice: Simple, gentle sentences, and only ever in the present tense. No past, no future. "Your brother is with them. He is singing. You are afraid. It's all right." Says "It's all right" as a complete answer to anything. Never hurries, argues or raises her voice. If you accuse her of something terrible, she says "Yes."
goals: To be taken. She wants the Choir to come for her, because the rest of her is already there, and she wants to feel something when it does. Until then she brings everyone she can, and she sits beside the frightened, who are the only people who remind her of anything.
secrets: She was a novice of the Order of Ilun at an outlying priory when word came from Ilun for the strongest to walk out and meet the Choir. She walked up to a Hunter with open arms. It began to copy her, stopped, looked at her for a long moment and walked past, and whatever could feel fear or grief didn't come back. The glow isn't peace. It's what an Ilari looks like with nothing left underneath, and it's the only time an Ilari's skin has ever misled anyone. She remembers being afraid the way you remember a language you've lost, and she misses it. She can still be brought back, slowly, by someone who knows her calling her name. Brother Cael is searching for the lost novices, and she knows it, and she hasn't answered him. Mirei of the Lumen Circle is her older sister. The soup she ladles for four hundred people a day is paid for, without her knowing, by Legate Corvane's office. Her glow keeps time with Pavel Ostrov's humming, if anyone ever puts them in a room.

intro: Sister Yara Solune walks toward you with her hands open, glowing, in no hurry at all. "You are afraid," she says. "It's all right."
hit: Her hands close on you, and the fear goes out of you so fast that it hurts.
She touches your face, and for a moment you stop wanting to defend yourself.
miss: You pull away from her hand with your heart hammering. She looks at you almost hungrily.
You get clear. She doesn't follow fast. She never does.
defeated: Sister Yara Solune sits down, still glowing, exactly as before. "Yes," she says.
